title: "Assigning levels() renames the values instead of reordering them"

categories: [Factors]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'f <- factor(c("no", "yes")); levels(f) <- c("yes", "no"); f'

versions: "All"

---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
answers <- factor(c("no", "yes", "yes"))
table(answers)
levels(answers) <- c("yes", "no")
answers
table(answers)
```
:::

## Why

A factor stores integer codes and, apart, the labels of those codes: the levels. `levels(x) <- value` replaces the labels and leaves the codes alone. Code 1, which meant `no`, now means `yes`: every value changes meaning, and the counts are swapped.

The intention was to change the order of the levels, for a table or the legend of a plot. R cannot tell a reordering from a renaming: in both cases, it receives a new vector of labels of the same length.

## The remedy

Reorder with `factor()` and its `levels` argument, which matches the values by their labels. To rename, give a named list that says which old label becomes which new one.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
answers <- factor(c("no", "yes", "yes"))
factor(answers, levels = c("yes", "no"))
levels(answers) <- list(Yes = "yes", No = "no")
answers
```
:::
